title: Marvell Investor Day pins AI custom-silicon ramp to H2 FY27, expands Google relationship
subtitle: The chip supplier used its October 6 event to put a date on the custom-ASIC acceleration and to signal more work with Google's TPU program.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Marvell held its Investor Day on October 6 and used the slot to put specifics on something it has been previewing for a quarter: the ramp in its custom-silicon business accelerates in the second half of fiscal 2027 (roughly mid-calendar 2026). CEO Matt Murphy walked analysts through a multi-year revenue outlook for the custom segment, which Marvell builds under contract for hyperscalers who want ASICs tuned to their own training or inference stacks rather than general-purpose GPUs. The company said the custom-silicon line should more than double next year.

The headline name attached to that ramp is Google. Marvell confirmed an expanded relationship on Google's TPU program — the lineage behind the Trillium and Ironwood accelerators that Google uses internally and sells through Google Cloud. The two companies have worked together on earlier TPU generations, but the Investor Day disclosure framed the collaboration as broader and more durable than prior public descriptions suggested. Marvell also highlighted data-center connectivity demand (optical DSPs, PAM4 transceivers) as a parallel growth driver, which matters because the chips are only useful if the fabric between them keeps up.

Custom silicon has quietly moved from a sidebar to the center of the AI-infrastructure story. OpenAI's Jalapeño (Broadcom), Anthropic's in-house silicon program with Samsung, Meta's MTIA, and Amazon's Trainium are all answers to the same question: can hyperscalers escape the Nvidia margin stack by designing their own accelerators? Marvell is the counterparty for several of those answers at once. The company is not a frontier-model shop, which is precisely why it keeps showing up in these transitions — it builds whichever ASIC the customer specifies, then sells the connectivity that stitches racks together.

A takeaway for learners: when a news cycle fixates on model releases, the chip layer under them often tells a more durable story. Custom silicon doesn't go viral, but it decides which labs can afford to serve how many users at what price. If you want to understand why GPT-6.1 Sol costs one-fifth of Astra, or why Anthropic can cut Opus 5.5 pricing 40%, start with the ASIC and interconnect roadmaps. Marvell's slide deck from today is a free primer on that layer, and the earnings transcripts that follow are better than any op-ed.
